issues.what: ffd_close_dstar is shipped at d = 0.2 (chosen on the first IS half) although the design defines d* on all IS bars, where d = 0.2 fails the ADF (stat -2.538 / -2.543 vs crit -2.862 on 1m / 5m) and d = 0.3 is the first to pass. The delivered series is therefore not stationary by the design's own rule and is in practice a price-level proxy: on 1m its Spearman correlation with raw close is 0.9993 (also 0.999 with open/high/low, room_edge, fz_band_lo/hi). The caveat records the one-step disagreement but not that the column behaves as a level/time proxy; the README column row still says 'chosen by ADF'.
issues.evidence: README ADF tables: minute d=0.2 all-IS -2.538 (pass False), d=0.3 -4.687 (pass True); 5minute d=0.2 all-IS -2.543 (False), d=0.3 -4.686 (True). Reproduced Spearman(ffd_close_dstar, close) = 0.9993 on the 5326 minute SETUP rows. The importance study already treats it as a time proxy (studies/importance/shortlist.py:26 'FFD of log close at d* = 0.2 (keeps most of the level)').
issues.fix: State in the README column row and in the FINDINGS caveat that the shipped d = 0.2 series fails the IS-wide ADF and correlates ~0.999 with the price level (a time proxy), or add the d = 0.3 column as a second candidate for the importance study to compare.
